question.text: This son of Henry the Fowler was crowned Holy Roman Emperor in 962. He defeated Magyar forces at Lechfeld.
question.clue: He had earlier thwarted Berengar, the king of Burgundy, by venturing into Italy a year before his coronation and marrying Adelaide, though he was drawn back to his homeland to put down a revolt by the Duke of Lotharingia, Conrad.

swap.text: The battles of Breteinfield and Lutzen took place during this major religious conflict, which lasted from 1618 to 1648.
swap.clue: This war's Bohemian phase ended at the Battle of White Mountain, which saw a victory for Count Tilly.

question.text: The title Emperor of the Romans would later morph into this position, holders of which were chosen by German Prince-Electors. Other holders of this title included Otto the Great and Frederick Barbarossa.
question.answerHtml: Holy Roman Emperor [accept German-Roman Emperor or Romanorum Imperator or Rex Romanorum; prompt on Emperor; do not accept or prompt on “Roman Emperor”]
question.clue: The Treaty of Pressburg invalidated this office after the battle of Austerlitz in 1806, and it was selected by seven electors after the 1356 Golden Bull.

swap.text: Through family ties, this Holy Roman Emperor also ruled Spain, the Netherlands, and Austria. He presided over the Diet of Worms, which outlawed Luther and the Reformation that had started during this man's reign.
swap.answerHtml: Charles V (accept Karl V or Carlos V; prompt on just “Charles” or “Carlos”; accept Charles I of Spain or Carlos I of Spain but do not accept or prompt on “Charles I”)
swap.clue: His general Charles of Lannoy secured the Treaty of Madrid for this man by defeating Francis I at Pavia.

question.text: Name this european leader who led 4 italian campaigns, and was nicknamed for his famously red beard.
question.answerHtml: Frederick Barbarossa (accept Frederick I , Friedrich I and Friedrich Barbarossa , prompt on Frederick or Friedrich alone)
question.clue: This man's body was preserved in a barrel of vinegar after this man had drowned in the Saleph River whilst leading his armies to the Third Crusade.

question.leadin: Events in Eastern Europe sometimes happen in threes.
question.text: Though chronologically the third, the Second event of this name provoked the Thirty Years' War, when two Imperial governors were cast out of a window from the Bohemian Chancellery.
question.clue: The first, in 1419, involved the killing of seven council members by a crowd of Hussites.

swap.text: The king of this territory served as the third elector. Frederick the Winter King ruled this territory during the 30 Years War, and it was earlier ruled by King Wenceslas.
swap.clue: A university in this region's New Town was founded by Charles IV, who was crowned after his blind father John died at the Battle of Crecy.

question.text: The third Holy Roman Emperor with this name was a close ally of the Piast king Boleslaw I. The first Holy Roman Emperor of this name, nicknamed "the Great," beat the Magyars at Lechfeld in 962.
question.answerHtml: Otto [or Otto III; or Otto I; or Otto the Great]
question.clue: The fourth and final one was the only Welf to become emperor, but was defeated at the Battle of Bouvines, after which Frederick II restored the Hohenstaufen Dynasty.

swap.text: In its aftermath, Frederick fled to Breslau and attempted to negotiate with Ferdinand. For 15 points, Christian Anhalt was defeated by the Catholic League under Tilly in what battle that ended the Bohemian phase of the Thirty Years War?

question.leadin: Answer some questions about the Lion of the north, Gustavus Adolphus.

question.text: had attempted to announce the rights he intended to enforce at this 1158 meeting near . He also hoped to restore the earlier suzerainty via the appointment of imperial officials.

question.text: This one-eyed general revolutionized mobile warfare by mounting cannons on armored wagons and led the Taborites to a series of victories over the Bohemian Crusade. After his 1424 death, Taborite leadership passed to Procop the Great.
question.clue: This one-eyed Taborite general, a reformist commander in the Hussite Wars, withstood Sigismund's siege of Prague at the Battle of Vitkov Hill. His tactics included arming wagon circles with cannons.
